page.title: Settings
page.purpose: Choose the active brand, set execution preferences, and see honestly what this machine can currently do. Owns locale switching per the template's responsive shell contract.

priorities.statement: The active brand is a first-class setting, because it changes every specimen on every surface.
priorities.notes: Switching brand re-renders the catalog. The setting shows which palette slots the selected brand defines, so an unresolvable style is predictable rather than discovered at compose time.

priorities.statement: Host capability is reported plainly, including what is unavailable.
priorities.notes: image-tools probes CPU, memory, GPU and VRAM to choose a model tier. Surfacing that here tells the operator why model-backed styles are slow, degraded, or refused — rather than leaving them to guess. Unknown VRAM is reported as unknown, never as zero.

priorities.statement: The free and metered boundary is stated, not implied.
priorities.notes: Which lanes cost money, and whether inference routes through a configured gateway or the operator's own keys, belongs where the operator can read it before spending.

states.description: Settings load without hiding the active theme and locale controls.
Known settings remain visible with a freshness notice.
Settings failure names the unavailable service and offers retry.
Available preferences remain editable while optional configuration is pending.
No optional configuration is present and the defaults are explained.
Brand, locale, theme, execution preference, and a host capability summary.
No brand is available from brand-manager. States that every style holding a palette slot will refuse to render, and routes to brand setup — rather than presenting an empty select.
The host can serve model-backed work locally. Reports the detected GPU and the model tier that would be selected.
The host cannot serve model-backed work. States that image-tools will route onward if a gateway route is configured, and that procedural styles are unaffected.
Neither local hardware nor a configured route can serve inference. States plainly that the procedural catalog still works in full, so the product is understood as usable rather than broken.
